name: Harare
subtitle: Harare, capital of Zimbabwe: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,427,209 people live in Harare Province (counted 2022).
The first British settlement on the site was named Fort Salisbury after the 3rd Marquess of Salisbury; the BSAC pioneer column reached the area in September 1890.
On the anniversary of independence in 1982 (18 April) Salisbury was renamed Harare, after the Shona chief Neharawa (SAHO spelling).

parts.text: The first British settlement on the site was named Fort Salisbury after the 3rd Marquess of Salisbury; the BSAC pioneer column reached the area in September 1890.
On the anniversary of independence in 1982 (18 April) Salisbury was renamed Harare, after the Shona chief Neharawa (SAHO spelling).
EBSCO gives the chief's name as Haarare and the renaming year as 1982; sources spell the chief's name differently.
Zimbabwe became independent in 1980; Salisbury remained the capital.
Harare Province holds the largest share of Zimbabwe's population, 16 percent in 2022.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Harare Province?

parts.text: 2,427,209 in 2022, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Harare Province (not the city alone), de facto count of people who spent census night 20 April 2022 in the province; preliminary results.

items.text: The British South Africa Company's pioneer column reaches the site; the settlement is named Fort Salisbury.
Salisbury becomes the capital of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland.
The Rhodes National Gallery opens in Salisbury (now the National Gallery of Zimbabwe).
Zimbabwe becomes independent; 2022 census was the fifth since independence.
Salisbury is renamed Harare on the anniversary of independence.
Zimbabwe holds its first digital census; census night is 20 April 2022.
